title: 第 3章 拜师第4 章 金手指
slug: 杀妖涨修为道爷我成了
lines: 清石踩着微光推开小院门，见沈回已站在院中，不由得一愣。
“沈师弟？你……一夜未睡？”清石揉了揉眼睛，上下打量他。
沈回笑着摇摇头：“睡过了，刚醒。”
清石见他神色清明，不似强撑，便也不再多问，只道：“那便好，随我来吧，莫让师父久等。”
两人穿过晨雾弥漫的庭院，石板路上凝着薄霜，踩上去发出细碎的“嚓嚓”声。
三清殿前的院子比昨夜看来更显空旷，清石引着沈回走向殿侧的一处抱厦，门楣上悬着块旧木匾，字迹漫漶，隐约能辨出“澄心”二字。
推门进去，里面比外头暖和些，却也不是暖炉熏烘的热，而是人多聚集带来的些许生气。
屋中立着个黄铜炭盆，炭火将熄未熄，只余一点暗红。正前方摆着一张简朴的长案，老道士已端坐其后，闭目养神。
案前地上，整整齐齐列放着六个蒲团。其中四个已坐了人，两男两女，皆着灰布道袍，背对着门口。
听到推门声，那四人齐刷刷回过头来。
靠左的是个身形高壮的中年男子，方脸阔口，目光炯炯；他旁边是个瘦削些的，面容白净，眼神灵动。
右侧两个女子，一个约莫二十出头，神情沉静；另一个看着小些，圆脸，眼睛乌溜溜地转，满是好奇。
四双眼睛齐齐落在沈回身上，带着毫不掩饰的打量。
“咳。”老道士并未睁眼，只轻咳一声。
那四人立刻转回头去，端正坐好，只是那圆脸少女还忍不住悄悄偏了偏脑袋。
清石忙拉着沈回在最外侧两个空蒲团上坐下，这蒲团填充得倒也厚实，沈回坐下时微微一陷。
“今日早课，诵《清净经》三遍。”
老道士睁开眼，声音平缓，“新来的，且听着。”
说罢，他不再看众人，自行拿起案上一卷略显古旧的经书，垂眸缓声念诵起来：“夫道者，有清有浊，有动有静。天清地浊，天动地静。降本流末，而生万物。清者浊之源，动者静之基。人能常清静，天地悉皆归……”
声音不高，却清晰沉稳，在安静的屋内悠悠回荡。
清石和其他四人显然熟稔，立刻跟上，合声诵念。声音参差却自有韵律，低低地汇在一处。
沈回坐在末位，翻看着眼前的经书，脸色有些茫然。
呃……不是说修道炼气么？怎的先念起经来了？
他连这世界通用的文字都尚且认不全，更别提拗口的经文。
可他见众人诵的专心，也不敢多问，只得垂着眼，努力去听那音节，默默记着调子，偶尔捕捉一两个似懂非懂的词句。
时间在低回的诵经声中缓缓流逝，炭盆里最后一点红光彻底熄灭，只剩灰白的余烬。
窗纸外的天光渐渐转亮，由青灰变为淡白。
三遍诵毕，老道士放下经卷。
“今日早课毕。尔等自去用斋。”
五人齐声称是，起身行礼。老道士却抬手虚按一下：“沈回，暂留片刻。”
正要退出的那五人脚步一顿，互相交换了个眼神，非但没走，反而磨磨蹭蹭挪到墙边，一副“我们就听听”的模样。
老道士瞥了他们一眼，倒也没出声驱赶。
待屋内重新安静，老道士目光落在沈回身上。
“你入我观中，尚未行拜师之礼。按规矩，未行礼前，只能算作居客，不可传法，只可随众诵经读书，做些杂事。”老道语气平缓，神色淡然。
沈回闻言，果断撩起道袍下摆，端端正正双膝跪地，俯身便拜：
content_en:
Qing Shi stepped on the dim light and pushed open the door of the small courtyard. When he saw Shen Hui standing in the courtyard, he couldn't help but be startled.
"Junior Brother Shen? You... didn't sleep all night?" Qingshi rubbed his eyes and looked him up and down.
Shen Hui smiled and shook his head: "I fell asleep and just woke up."
Qingshi saw that his expression was clear and clear, and he didn't seem to be forcing himself, so he stopped asking any more questions and just said: "That's fine, come with me, don't keep Master waiting."
The two walked through the courtyard filled with morning mist. There was a thin layer of frost on the stone pavement, which made a tiny "chuck" sound when they stepped on it.
The courtyard in front of the Sanqing Hall seemed even more empty than last night. Qingshi led Shen Hui to a small building on the side of the hall. There was an old wooden plaque hanging on the lintel with smeared handwriting, and the word "Chengxin" could be vaguely discerned.
Pushing the door open and going in, it's warmer inside than outside, but it's not the heat from the stove, but a bit of life brought by the gathering of people.
There was a brass charcoal basin standing in the middle of the room. The charcoal fire was almost extinguished but only a little dark red remained. There was a simple long table in front of him, and the old Taoist priest was sitting behind it, closing his eyes and relaxing.
On the ground in front of the case, six futons were neatly placed. Four of them were already occupied, two men and two women, both wearing gray preaching robes, with their backs to the door.
Hearing the sound of the door being pushed open, the four people all turned around.
The person on the left is a tall, middle-aged man with a square face, a wide mouth, and bright eyes; next to him is a thinner man with a fair face and lively eyes.
There are two women on the right, one is in her early twenties, with a calm expression; the other is smaller, with a round face and dark eyes, full of curiosity.
Four pairs of eyes all fell on Shen Hui, looking at him unabashedly.
"Cough." The old Taoist priest did not open his eyes, but coughed lightly.
The four people immediately turned back and sat upright, but the round-faced girl couldn't help but tilt her head quietly.
Qingshi hurriedly pulled Shen Hui and sat down on the two outermost empty futons. The futons were quite thickly filled, and Shen Hui sank slightly when he sat down.
"Today's morning class, recite the Purity Sutra three times."
The old Taoist priest opened his eyes and said in a calm voice, "Newcomer, please listen."
After that, he stopped looking at the crowd and picked up an ancient scripture on his desk. He lowered his eyes and began to recite slowly: "In the way of husband, there is purity and turbidity, movement and stillness. The sky is clear and the earth is turbid, and the sky is moving and the earth is quiet. All things come into being at the end of the original flow. The pure is the source of turbidity, and the movement is the foundation of stillness. If people can always be quiet, heaven and earth will all return..."
The voice was not high, but clear and steady, echoing slowly in the quiet room.
Qingshi and the other four people were obviously familiar with it, and immediately followed it, chanting in unison. The sounds were uneven but had their own rhythm, low and low.
Shen Hui sat in the last seat, looking at the scriptures in front of him, his face a little confused.
Uh... isn't it about cultivating Taoism and refining Qi? Why did you start reciting the sutra first?
He can't even recognize all the characters commonly used in this world, let alone the difficult-to-pronounce scriptures.
But seeing how attentive everyone was in reciting, he didn't dare to ask any more questions. He could only lower his eyes and try hard to listen to the syllables, memorizing the tune silently, and occasionally catching one or two words that he seemed to understand but didn't understand.
…
Time passed slowly amidst the low sound of chanting, and the last red light in the charcoal basin was completely extinguished, leaving only gray embers.
The skylight outside the window paper gradually turned brighter, changing from blue gray to pale white.
After reciting it three times, the old Taoist priest put down the scripture.
"Morning class is over today. You guys go and have your meal."
The five of them all claimed yes and stood up to salute. The old Taoist priest raised his hand and pressed it softly: "Shen Hui, stay here for a moment."
The five people who were about to exit paused and exchanged glances with each other. Instead of leaving, they moved slowly to the wall, looking like "Let's just listen."
The old Taoist priest glanced at them but didn't say anything to drive them away.
When the room became quiet again, the old Taoist priest's eyes fell on Shen Hui.
"When you enter my temple, you have not yet performed the rituals of becoming a disciple. According to the rules, before you have performed the rituals, you can only be regarded as a guest and cannot teach the Dharma. You can only chant sutras, read books, and do other chores with the crowd." The old Taoist said in a calm tone and looked calm.
When Shen Hui heard this, he decisively lifted up the hem of his Taoist robe, knelt down on his knees upright, and bowed down:
